dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: The tracker's three existing pages (index, /queue, /stats) have no at-a-glance operational view; two real incidents already happened because of this — the auto-publish workflow failed silently on its first 3 hourly runs (2026-09-25) before anyone noticed, and a 30-idea batch drifted to a 28/2 reframe/observational split before manual correction (internal-docs/ideas-tracker/dashboard-next-session-prompt.md, auto-publish-credentials.md).

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Opening a new /dashboard route shows, on one page, refreshed automatically every 60s via partial DOM updates: the next auto_publish idea to post, the last 5 posts with cached engagement + Instagram link, the last 5 freshly-added ideas, stalled 'scripted' drafts (3+ days untouched) with direct links, time since the last successful pipeline heartbeat, current register balance, backlog size + days-since-last-post, and an upcoming-week calendar of auto_publish-scheduled ideas.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Thirteen pass/fail criteria after a success-criteria critic pass fixed a wrong DB filename, an under-asserting criterion, two checks wrongly marked judgment instead of cmd, and added missing content-correctness and auth-behavior checks; only the visual polling-cadence check remains judgment.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: In/out boundaries settled across seven interview rounds plus a hidden-dependency critic pass that found the originally-planned firewall step was a no-op (n8n's API is deliberately loopback-only) and replaced it with a heartbeat n8n pushes to the tracker after every run — reusing the pipeline's existing outbound connection instead of opening any new network path, and removing the only manual/non-automatable step from scope entirely.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: The pipeline-health widget is now a pure local-DB read like the other 7 widgets, so the earlier external-dependency tension is resolved by design rather than by a graceful-degradation branch; n8n's deliberate loopback-only hardening from the auto-publish project is preserved untouched.

problem: The ideas tracker's homepage today is purely operational in the narrowest sense — a quick-add form plus a filterable list of every idea. /queue shows status='ready' ideas and /stats shows backward-looking performance analytics, but nothing answers, at a glance, what's about to publish, what just posted, what's freshly added and needs review, or whether the auto-publish pipeline is actually healthy.

This gap already cost real visibility: the auto-publish n8n workflow's first 3 hourly executions (2026-09-25, 15:00/16:00/17:00 UTC) all failed with 401 on a stale Basic Auth credential, discovered by accident while verifying an unrelated credential swap, not through any monitoring (internal-docs/ideas-tracker/auto-publish-credentials.md).

Separately, a 30-idea batch loaded the same day initially produced a 28/2 reframe:observational split against the account's documented ~6:4 target, caught and corrected manually rather than surfaced by the app itself.
goals: Opening /dashboard shows, without navigating to any other page: the next auto_publish idea due to post and when; the last 5 posts with their cached engagement numbers and a link to view them on Instagram; the last 5 freshly-added ideas; stalled 'scripted' drafts idle 3+ days with direct links; time since the last successful pipeline heartbeat (and its status); the current rolling register balance; backlog size and days since the last post; and an upcoming-week mini-calendar of auto_publish-scheduled ideas.
The page refreshes this data automatically roughly every 60 seconds via a JS-polling partial DOM update, without a full page reload.

successCriteria.criterion: An unauthenticated GET to /dashboard redirects to /login, matching every other page route in this app
An unauthenticated GET to /dashboard/widgets returns a bare 401 (not an HTML redirect), so the polling JS can detect an expired session and redirect the whole page itself

An authenticated GET to /dashboard renders all 8 named widget sections (next-to-publish, just-posted, freshly-added, needs-review, pipeline-health, register-balance, quick-stats [backlog + days-since-last-post], calendar)

check.cmd: TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/login -d "username=$DASH_USER" -d "password=$DASH_PASS" | jq -r .token); N=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/dashboard | grep -o 'data-widget="[a-z-]*"' | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' '); [ "$N" = "8" ]

successCriteria.criterion: GET /dashboard/widgets returns the same 8 named sections as a bare HTML fragment (no page chrome), so client-side JS can swap it in without client-side templating

check.cmd: TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/login -d "username=$DASH_USER" -d "password=$DASH_PASS" | jq -r .token); N=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/dashboard/widgets | grep -o 'data-widget="[a-z-]*"' | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' '); [ "$N" = "8" ]

successCriteria.criterion: The next-to-publish widget shows the actual next auto_publish idea (soonest scheduled_at among non-terminal statuses), or an explicit empty state when none exist

check.cmd: EXPECTED=$(sqlite3 web/pancracio.db "SELECT id FROM ideas WHERE auto_publish=1 AND status NOT IN ('posted','failed','archived') ORDER BY (scheduled_at IS NULL), scheduled_at ASC LIMIT 1"); TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/login -d "username=$DASH_USER" -d "password=$DASH_PASS" | jq -r .token); curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/dashboard | grep -q "data-next-idea-id=\"$EXPECTED\""
check.expect: exits 0 (if EXPECTED is empty, the widget instead renders an explicit 'nothing scheduled' state)

successCriteria.criterion: The just-posted widget's 5 entries match the tracker's actual 5 most recent posts, not stale/hardcoded data

check.cmd: TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/login -d "username=$DASH_USER" -d "password=$DASH_PASS" | jq -r .token); A=$(sqlite3 web/pancracio.db "SELECT id FROM posts ORDER BY posted_at DESC LIMIT 5"); B=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/dashboard | grep -o 'data-post-id="[0-9]*"' | cut -d'"' -f2); [ "$A" = "$B" ]

successCriteria.criterion: The freshly-added widget's 5 entries match the 5 most recent status='idea' ideas

check.cmd: TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/login -d "username=$DASH_USER" -d "password=$DASH_PASS" | jq -r .token); A=$(sqlite3 web/pancracio.db "SELECT id FROM ideas WHERE status='idea' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 5"); B=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/dashboard | grep -o 'data-fresh-idea-id="[0-9]*"' | cut -d'"' -f2); [ "$A" = "$B" ]

successCriteria.criterion: The needs-review widget lists exactly the ideas with status='scripted' untouched (updated_at) for 3+ days

check.cmd: TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/login -d "username=$DASH_USER" -d "password=$DASH_PASS" | jq -r .token); A=$(sqlite3 web/pancracio.db "SELECT id FROM ideas WHERE status='scripted' AND datetime(updated_at) <= datetime('now','-3 days') ORDER BY updated_at ASC"); B=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/dashboard | grep -o 'data-stalled-idea-id="[0-9]*"' | cut -d'"' -f2); [ "$A" = "$B" ]

successCriteria.criterion: The calendar widget shows exactly the auto_publish ideas scheduled in the next 7 days

check.cmd: TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/login -d "username=$DASH_USER" -d "password=$DASH_PASS" | jq -r .token); A=$(sqlite3 web/pancracio.db "SELECT id FROM ideas WHERE auto_publish=1 AND datetime(scheduled_at) BETWEEN datetime('now') AND datetime('now','+7 days') ORDER BY scheduled_at ASC"); B=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/dashboard | grep -o 'data-calendar-idea-id="[0-9]*"' | cut -d'"' -f2); [ "$A" = "$B" ]

successCriteria.criterion: The quick-stats widget's backlog size AND days-since-last-post both match direct DB queries

check.cmd: BACKLOG=$(sqlite3 web/pancracio.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ideas WHERE status NOT IN ('posted','archived')"); DAYS=$(sqlite3 web/pancracio.db "SELECT CAST(julianday('now')-julianday(MAX(posted_at)) AS INT) FROM posts"); TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/login -d "username=$DASH_USER" -d "password=$DASH_PASS" | jq -r .token); PAGE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/dashboard); echo "$PAGE" | grep -q "data-backlog-count=\"$BACKLOG\"" && echo "$PAGE" | grep -q "data-days-since-post=\"$DAYS\""

successCriteria.criterion: The register-balance widget's counts match the existing GET /internal/register-counts endpoint exactly

check.cmd: TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/login -d "username=$DASH_USER" -d "password=$DASH_PASS" | jq -r .token); A=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/internal/register-counts | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps(json.load(sys.stdin), sort_keys=True))'); B=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/dashboard | grep -o 'data-register-counts="[^"]*"' | cut -d'"' -f2 | python3 -c 'import json,sys,html; print(json.dumps(json.loads(html.unescape(sys.stdin.read())), sort_keys=True))'); [ "$A" = "$B" ]

successCriteria.criterion: The pipeline-health widget correctly reflects the heartbeat table's state: an explicit 'no data yet' state before any heartbeat exists, and the real status/timestamp after one is recorded

check.cmd: TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/login -d "username=$DASH_USER" -d "password=$DASH_PASS" | jq -r .token); curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/internal/pipeline-heartbeat -d 'status=success' > /dev/null; curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/dashboard | grep -q 'data-pipeline-status="success"'

successCriteria.criterion: The dashboard refreshes its widgets roughly every 60 seconds via a JS-polling partial DOM update, without a full page reload

check.judgment: With the dashboard open and browser devtools' Network tab visible, confirm a GET to /dashboard/widgets fires approximately every 60s, and that the page does not do a full navigation/reload each time.

mvp.item: New GET /dashboard route (index.html and every other existing page/route unchanged)
mvp.reason: Lowest-risk placement — nothing that currently works changes; the dashboard becomes an additional entry point, reachable via a new nav link.

mvp.item: Next-to-publish widget: single soonest idea where auto_publish=1 AND status NOT IN ('posted','failed','archived'), ordered by scheduled_at
mvp.reason: Closes the exact gap named in the source doc — /queue's status='ready' filter doesn't show this. Scoped to a single item since the calendar widget covers the multi-day view.

mvp.item: Just-posted widget: last 5 posts newest-first, with cached engagement numbers (likes/comments/etc.) and a link to the live Instagram post via the existing post_url column
mvp.reason: Reuses existing posts table columns; avoids a new live Instagram API call on a page that's otherwise pure local-DB reads.

mvp.item: Freshly-added widget: last 5 ideas with status='idea', newest-first, reusing the existing _get_ideas(status='idea', sort='newest') helper capped at 5 rows rather than a bespoke query
mvp.reason: Directly answers 'what needs review/scheduling' for newly captured ideas (e.g. the 30-idea batch from 2026-09-25), and the exact same query already backs the homepage's own filter — no reason to duplicate it.

mvp.item: Needs-review widget: ideas with status='scripted' untouched (updated_at) for 3+ days, with direct links to each
mvp.reason: Catches a different failure mode than 'freshly added' — drafts that got started and then forgotten.

mvp.item: Pipeline-health widget: shows time since the last successful pipeline heartbeat and its status (success/failed)
mvp.reason: Directly targets the exact incident that already happened (3 silent failures), as a pure local-DB read — no external call, no graceful-degradation branch needed.

mvp.item: New POST /internal/pipeline-heartbeat endpoint recording the latest heartbeat status + timestamp (a new minimal table, e.g. pipeline_heartbeats, or a settings-table key)
mvp.reason: Gives the dashboard a local signal it can always read, instead of reaching out to n8n's (deliberately loopback-only) API.

mvp.item: One additional node appended to n8n/workflows/auto-publish.json, POSTing to /internal/pipeline-heartbeat at the end of each run (success or failure path) via the existing write-scoped n8n API key, then re-exported and committed per this project's established convention
mvp.reason: n8n already calls the tracker every hour in this same direction (outbound from bulbasaur); this adds one more call rather than opening any new inbound network path, and preserves n8n's deliberate loopback-only hardening from the auto-publish project untouched.

mvp.item: Register-balance widget: reuse the existing _get_recent_register_counts() helper
mvp.reason: Already computes exactly this; directly reusable per the source doc, no new query needed.

mvp.item: Quick-stats widget combining backlog size (count of ideas not in posted/archived) and days since last post (from MAX(posts.posted_at)) in one rendered section
mvp.reason: Both are single cheap numbers the user explicitly asked for; grouping them keeps the total widget count at 8 distinct sections instead of 9 near-identical single-number cards.

mvp.item: Upcoming-week mini-calendar: auto_publish-scheduled ideas over the next 7 days
mvp.reason: Scoped to auto_publish only, matching the next-to-publish widget, so the page tells one consistent story about what this app itself controls.

mvp.item: GET /dashboard/widgets partial-update endpoint, rendering the same 8 widget sections as a bare HTML fragment via the existing Jinja templates, returning 401 (not a login redirect) when unauthenticated
mvp.reason: Lets client-side JS refresh data via an innerHTML swap without introducing client-side templating, keeping the app Jinja-only everywhere; a bare 401 lets the polling JS detect an expired session itself.

mvp.item: Client-side JS polling /dashboard/widgets every 60s and swapping the result into the page
mvp.reason: User's explicit choice for a genuinely live-feeling page over a plain reload-to-refresh model, accepting this as the app's first real client-side data-fetching logic.
Makes the new route discoverable, matching how Queue/Stats/Settings are already linked.

mvp.item: A dedicated test/fixture account, created via the existing scripts/create_user.py, for verification checks that need an authenticated session
mvp.reason: Success-criteria checks need a real, non-placeholder way to authenticate; this matches the project's own established account-provisioning path.

outOfScope.item: Replacing the homepage ('/') with the dashboard
outOfScope.reason: Explicitly declined — keeps this a strictly additive, lowest-risk change; the quick-add + full list experience stays exactly as it is today.

outOfScope.item: Including manually-scheduled (non-auto_publish) ideas in the next-to-publish or calendar widgets
outOfScope.reason: Explicitly declined — keeps this page describing only what the app itself controls via the auto_publish pipeline, avoiding mixing two different scheduling mechanisms in one view.

outOfScope.item: Live Instagram Graph API calls on dashboard page load
outOfScope.reason: Explicitly declined — avoids a new dependency, latency, and rate-limit risk on a page meant to be checked frequently; cached values plus the existing manual per-post Refresh button are sufficient.

outOfScope.item: Querying n8n's REST API directly from the tracker (via firewall change, SSH tunnel, or rebinding n8n's Docker port)
outOfScope.reason: n8n's API is deliberately loopback-only per the auto-publish project's own hardening decision; a heartbeat push achieves the same visibility goal without touching that decision or adding new network infrastructure.

outOfScope.item: A PRD layer between this contract and the implementation spec
outOfScope.reason: Single-developer personal tool with no external stakeholder sign-off step; the spec is sufficient.

outOfScope.item: A new automated test suite / pytest for this app
outOfScope.reason: This app has no existing test infrastructure; introducing one is a separate concern from this feature.

decisions.rejected: Replace '/' with the dashboard, moving quick-add elsewhere
decisions.reason: Lowest risk — nothing existing changes; the dashboard is purely additive.

decisions.decision: Next-to-publish and calendar widgets scoped to auto_publish=1 ideas only
decisions.rejected: Also include manually-scheduled (Meta Business Suite) posts
decisions.reason: Keeps one consistent story on the page — what this app itself controls — rather than mixing two different scheduling mechanisms.

decisions.decision: Pipeline health via a heartbeat n8n pushes to the tracker after every run
decisions.rejected: Querying n8n's REST API directly from the tracker — via a firewall change, a persistent SSH tunnel, or rebinding n8n's Docker port off loopback
decisions.reason: A hidden-dependency critic pass found n8n's API is deliberately loopback-only (an explicit prior decision in the auto-publish project, made so nothing outside the VPS could ever reach it). A heartbeat push reuses the exact outbound connection direction the pipeline already uses every hour, so it needs no new network exposure and no new always-running tunnel process, and it leaves that prior hardening decision completely untouched.

decisions.decision: Cached DB engagement values + existing post_url link for the just-posted widget
decisions.rejected: Live-fetch engagement from the Instagram Graph API on every dashboard load
decisions.reason: Zero new dependency or latency risk; matches the app's existing manual-refresh-per-post pattern.

decisions.decision: JS polling every 60s against a new /dashboard/widgets endpoint, swapping in a server-rendered HTML fragment
decisions.reason: User wanted a smoother, non-flashing live-feeling page over the simplest zero-JS option, accepting this as the app's first real client-side data-fetching logic.

decisions.decision: The polling endpoint returns a server-rendered HTML fragment (reusing existing Jinja templates)
decisions.rejected: A JSON API with client-side JS building the DOM/HTML
decisions.reason: Keeps the app Jinja-only everywhere, avoiding introducing client-side templating for the first time.

decisions.rejected: "Ready but missing final_image_path" (the existing per-card guardrail) or combining both conditions
decisions.reason: Catches a distinct failure mode (stalled drafts) that the 'freshly added' widget can't see, without duplicating the guardrail already shown per-card on Queue.

decisions.decision: Next-to-publish widget shows a single item
decisions.rejected: A short list of the next 3-5 upcoming auto_publish ideas
decisions.reason: The upcoming-week calendar widget already covers the multi-day view, so a list here would duplicate it.

decisions.decision: Backlog size and days-since-last-post render together in one 'quick stats' widget section
decisions.reason: Both are single cheap numbers; combining them keeps the total distinct widget count at 8 instead of 9 near-identical single-number cards.

decisions.decision: Freshly-added widget reuses the existing _get_ideas(status='idea', sort='newest') helper capped at 5 rows
decisions.reason: A success-criteria critic pass noted this is the exact same query the homepage's own filter already runs; no reason to duplicate it.

decisions.decision: Register-balance and pipeline-health success criteria are written as cmd checks
decisions.reason: A success-criteria critic pass found both compare two already-curlable/queryable sources mechanically — no human eyeballing needed.

decisions.decision: Modifying the live n8n workflow (adding the heartbeat node) is done via n8n's existing write-scoped REST API as part of the build, then re-exported to git
decisions.rejected: Treat it as a manual step for the user to do by hand in the n8n UI
decisions.reason: This project's own established precedent (the Basic-Auth-to-bearer-token credential swap) already did live workflow edits this way; it's an application-level workflow change, not a system/security-setting change like the firewall step it replaces.

phases.title: Dashboard route, widgets, heartbeat, and polling
phases.notes: Single-phase project: new /dashboard + /dashboard/widgets routes, all 8 widget sections (with the quick-stats and pipeline-health widgets as pure local-DB reads), the new /internal/pipeline-heartbeat endpoint + minimal schema addition, one new node appended to n8n/workflows/auto-publish.json (via n8n's REST API, then re-exported), the nav link, and client-side polling JS in a new web/static/dashboard.js.
